newsitem.title: USA: Georgia Power Vogtle 2 power plant trips off.
newsitem.headline: Georgia Power Vogtle 2 power plant trips off.

text.p: Problems with a feedwater pump at Georgia Power Co's 1,162 megawatt (MW) Vogtle 2 nuclear power plant caused the unit to trip off line, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Thursday.
The unit had been operating at 64 percent of capacity at the time it tripped about 1830 EDT Wednesday, the NRC said.

According to the report filed by the operator with the NRC, the trip was triggered when one of the main feedwater pumps failed, causing a loss of the main condensor vacuum and, in turn, causing the turbine to automatically shut down.

The unit had been operating at reduced capacity while engineers worked to correct feed pump vibrations. The company said Wednesday they had expected to have the unit running at full capacity by Friday.
No word was immediately available on when the unit would likely return to service.
Georgia Power is a subsidiary of the Southern Co.
Oglethorpe Power Corp has a 30 percent stake in the Vogtle plant, with the Municipal Electric Authority of Georgia holding 22.7 percent and the City of Dalton, Ga., holding 1.6 percent.
The Vogtle facility is in Waynesboro, Ga.
